problem: Open-vocabulary semantic mapping and navigation systems such as ConceptFusion, ConceptGraphs, HOV-SG and Clio have three shortcomings for language-specified navigation in large, unknown, unstructured environments. They rely on image-segmentation priors, which yield sparse object-level semantics, and they are limited to indoor or building scale. Most are also not vision-only or not real-time. Separately, 3DGS SLAM methods (MonoGS, RTG-SLAM, Gaussian-SLAM, LoopSplat) run out of GPU memory at large scale because they do not properly offload and reload submaps.
motivation: Robots doing field tasks (inspection, search-and-rescue) must build a map online that is rich enough to answer tasks that may be re-specified or underspecified, and they must do it on SWaP-constrained hardware with only a stereo camera. Outdoor scenes have few distinct objects, so dense continuous language features beat object-level labels there. Dense 3DGS maps with 512-d features are too large for memory and too slow for real-time planning and collision checking. This motivates feature compression, submapping and a sparse hierarchy on top of the dense map.
key_idea: Store PCA-compressed dense CLIP-DINOiser features in every Gaussian of an online, submapped 3DGS map. Build a sparse submap/region/object hierarchy by metric-semantic agglomerative clustering, run a budgeted graph planner over task-relevance scores on that hierarchy, and use the dense Gaussians for chance-constrained collision checking in a motion-primitive trajectory planner.
insight: Dense per-Gaussian language features built without segmentation priors hold up well in unstructured outdoor scenes. Outdoors, ATLAS reaches 0.30 2D mIOU against 0.19 for HOV-SG, while staying roughly competitive indoors on ScanNet (0.15 vs 0.22 mIOU) at 0.21 s/frame versus 5-8.6 s for the baselines. A simple scene-agnostic linear PCA (512→24 d, fit on COCO) keeps cosine similarity at about 0.95 to the original features, avoiding scene-specific autoencoders that cannot be used during exploration. Scalability comes from explicit submap load/unload and anchor-pose updates. GPU memory is 9.68 GB versus 21.33 GB for LoopSplat, and MonoGS and RTG-SLAM fail outright. Loop-closure anchor updates raise PSNR from 12.62 to 14.31. Collision checking grows linearly with the number of Gaussians (over 1 s at 10M), which justifies the local-map radius and the chance-constrained r*.
method: Language-embedded 3DGS (SplaTAM-based): each Gaussian stores position, isotropic variance, RGB, opacity and an m=24-d feature. The map is fit online at 1 Hz with L1 color, depth and feature rendering losses, using ZED 2i VIO poses and 320×240 stereo RGB-D with depth capped at 5 m.

Feature compression: dense per-pixel CLIP-DINOiser features (MaskCLIP refined with DINOv2 localization priors, CLIP ViT-B/16, 512-d) are projected to 24-d with an incremental PCA fit offline on COCO 2017. Features are decoded with inverse PCA when scoring task relevance.

Submapping with tectonic anchors: Gaussians are stored relative to per-submap SE(3) anchor poses (radius 2 m indoor, 5 m outdoor). Submaps within R_map=10 m are loaded on the GPU and others are offloaded. After loop closure/PGO only the anchors are updated, not the Gaussians.

Metric-semantic agglomerative clustering: when a submap is offloaded, about 5,000 sampled Gaussians are clustered with the distance ||x−x'|| + λ(1−cos(f,f')) into a depth-3 tree (≤100 leaves, root degree ≤4 outdoors). Leaf CLIP-text relevance is summed up the tree to region and submap scores, which enables cheap re-tasking. In the loaded local map, relevance is computed on a 0.1 m grid.

Hierarchical discrete planner (0.2 Hz): a budget-constrained, utility-maximizing path over the submap graph is found with a priority-queue search pruned by the travel budget. Dijkstra then refines it over the region nodes of the selected submaps into a reference path with local goals at most 5 m away.

Continuous planner (1 Hz): A* over unicycle motion primitives with cost λΔt+(v²+ω²)Δt, using parallelized GPU collision checks against the Gaussians. A union-bound chance constraint (δ=0.001, density ρ=1250/m³) gives the radius r*=5 m beyond which Gaussians can be ignored.
Task termination: when masked pixel relevance exceeds a threshold, LLaVA-OneVision is queried with the image and task and returns yes/no plus a scene description.

setting.backbone: CLIP-DINOiser (CLIP ViT-B/16 + DINOv2, frozen) features with PCA; CLIP text encoder for task relevance; LLaVA-OneVision (frozen) for termination; classical graph search + motion-primitive A* for decisions
setting.training_data: none (training-free); PCA encoder fit offline on COCO 2017 images
setting.observation: stereo RGB-D from ZED 2i (320×240, depth ≤5 m) + visual-inertial odometry
setting.action_space: continuous unicycle trajectories from motion primitives over (v, ω), with local goals from the discrete planner
setting.simulator: real world only (component ablations offline on ScanNet, HM3D scene 00824 and self-collected robot data)
setting.privileged: none for online runs (VIO odometry only; LiDAR used only for evaluation GT). Outdoor1 uses a pre-built map from a prior teleoperated run.

numbers_note: No standard embodied-navigation benchmark (HM3D-ObjNav, etc.) is evaluated. Navigation results are 7 single-run real-world experiments reported as path length and competitive ratios. The per-experiment table gives SP ratios 0.48, 0.71, –, 0.48, 0.67, 0.64, 0.55 and GT ratios 0.41, 0.68, 0.99, 0.46, 0.62, 0.64, 0.53. No success rate is reported and no navigation baseline is compared. The PCA ablation (cosine similarity 0.9529 at 24-d on ScanNet) and collision-check timing are given only in figures. Segmentation metrics were printed as fractions and are converted to 0-100 here.
results: On a Clearpath Jackal with only a ZED 2i stereo camera, ATLAS ran 7 language-specified navigation tasks covering more than 2 km and 47,000 m², building maps of up to 11.28M Gaussians online. It achieved competitive ratios of about 0.59 (vs shortest path on the final graph) and 0.56 (vs GPS ground truth), and 0.99 when a pre-built map was given. Among the baseline mapping methods, it beats HOV-SG, ConceptGraphs and ConceptFusion on outdoor dense segmentation (mIOU 0.30 vs best 0.19; PSNR 20.69 vs 6.87). On ScanNet it trails HOV-SG in mIOU (0.15 vs 0.22) but is over 40× faster (0.21 vs 8.58 s/frame) and uses less memory. It also uses less than half of LoopSplat's GPU memory on HM3D 00824.
limitations: Each real-robot experiment is run once, with no navigation baselines and no standard simulated benchmark, so statistical repeatability and comparative navigation performance are not established.
Heavily dependent on external VIO and stereo depth quality: drift, textureless ground and harsh sunlight degrade the map, and loop closure depends on the external estimator.
CLIP-similarity relevance with PCA features struggles with abstract tasks (e.g. 'find a place to rest') that need LLM decomposition; only largely planar, single-floor environments are tested.
